TO 

IS 2894 : 1987 SPECIFICATION FOR WOODEN HANDLES 

FOR WOOD WORKING CHISELS AND GOUGES

(Page 5, clause 5.1) — Add the following line at the beginning of the clause: 

'The wooden handles are classified into five sizes on the basis of their overall dimension 'A' and ferrule 
dimension 'B' (see Fig. 1).' 

(Page 5, clauses 6 and 6.1) — Delete the clauses and renumber clauses 7, 7.1 and 7.2 as 6, 6.1 and 6.2 
respectively. 

(Page 5, clause 7) — Add the following new clauses: 

'1 TESTS

Reprography Unit, BIS, New Delhi, India 



IS : 2894 - 1987 

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 

WOODEN HANDLES FOR 

WOOD WORKING CHISELS AND GOUGES 

( First Revision ) 

0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau 
of Indian Standards on 28 June 1987, after the draft finalized by the 
Timber Stores Sectional Committee had been approved by the Civil 
Engineering Division Council. 

0.2 This standard was originally published in 1965. The general require- 
ments for wooden tool handles are covered by IS : 620-1985*. A series 
of standards has been prepared for various hand tools and for the cor- 
responding wooden handles for use with these hand tools, another series 
of standards has been prepared. This standard deals with wooden 
handles for wood working chisels and gouges conforming to IS : 1930 
( Parts 1 to 5 ) - I975t. In the present revision, dimensions oi the 
handles have been standardized and tabulated irrespective of their end 
use. Clause on treatment of handles has been modified to bring in line 
with other pubHshed standards. 

0.3 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of 
this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, 
expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS : 2 - 1960t. The number of significant places retained in the rounded 
off value -should be the same as that of the specified value in this 
standard. 



1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard covers the requirements of 5 sizes of wooden handles 
for wood working chisels and gouges, both ends with MS seamless or 
welded ferrules. 



♦General requirements for wooden tool handles ( fourth revision ). 
tSpecification for chisels and gouges: Parts 1 to 5, 
JRules for rounding off numerical values ( revised). 



IS : 2894 - 1987 

2. TERMINOLOGY 

2,1 For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given in IS : 707- 
1976* shall apply. 

3. MATERIALS 

3.1 Timber — Any of the timbers specified for class V handles in 
IS : 620 - 1985t. 

3.1.1 The blanks shall be well seasoned ( preferably air-seasoned ) 
to a moisture content not exceeding 15 percent and the inclination of 
the grain shall not exceed 1 in 20, They shall be free from centre 
heart ( pith ), any kind of decay ( rot ), checks, shakes, splits ( except 
hair splits ), borer holes, warp and any other defect except those 
permitted in the finished handles ( see IS : 620 - 1985t ). 

3*2 Mild Steel — 1'6 ± 0'2 mm thick and 2'5 ± 0*3 mm thick sheets 
or seamless tubes. 

4. MANUFACTURE 

4.1 The handles shall be made to the shape and design as shown in 
Fig. 1. 

4.2 The ferrules shall be either made from seamless tube or from sheet 
butt welded and shall be fitted to the handles as shown in Fig. 1. 



FERRULE MS SEAMLESS TUBES 
OR WELDED 1-6+ 0'2mfn THICK 



FERRULE, MS SEAML ESS TUBES 
OR WELDED 2-5+ 0'3mm THICK- 




FiG. 1 Typical Sketch of Wooden Handle for Chisels and 
Gouges

revision ). 

tOeneral requirements for wooden tool handles {fourth revision ). 



IS : 2894 - 1987

given in Table 1 read with Fig. 1.

6. TOLERANCES 

6.1 Normal engineering tolerances shall be permissible. 

7. WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 

7.1 The ferrules shall be tight fit to the handles. If welded, welding 
shall be clean and sound. 

7.2 The handles shall be finished reasonably smooth. 

8. TREATMENT 

8.1 Unless otherwise specified by the purchaser, immediately after 
inspection all accepted tool handles shall be thoroughly soaked in hot 
( about 90''C ) raw linseed oil for one hour and allowed to drain. They 
shall then to wiped clean with a dry piece of cloth. Ferrules shall be 
brushed with red oxide. 



9. MARKING 

9,1 Unless otherwise specified, each handle shall be legibly and indelibly 
marked with the manufacturer's name or recognized trade-mark and 
year of manufacture. 



IS : 2894 - 1987 

9.1.1 The handles may also be marked with the Standard Mark. 

Note — The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made there- 
under. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys 
the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of 
that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality 
control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. 
Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for con- 
formity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under 
which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufac- 
turers or producers, may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
